selection: MERLIN_TARGET_PATH selects support explicitly and always wins. Unset, each target's in-repo provider under examples/<example>/support is selected, plus each pinned_support package fetched at exactly its pinned commit (out/build/generated/pinned/<target>@<sha12>), all keyed by provider.yaml target, never by directory name; a pinned package that is not fetched is an error naming its setup command, never a fallback. An empty value selects none. Historical companion paths are provenance, never runtime defaults.
qualification_scope: Read-only provider identity, exact source SHA256 parity, plugin reference existence, schema diagnostic parity. No hardware execution or compiler qualification.
candidate_boundary: Support plugins are experimenter-side answer-bearing code, not candidate payload. Every in-repo examples/*/support tree, canonical or vendored, and every fetched pinned_support checkout under out/build/generated/pinned/ (any revision, its submodules included), is an answer surface whatever MERLIN_TARGET_PATH selects: agent sandboxes, bundle snapshots and clean rooms withhold it (only an explicit contracts/ grant can reach inside, and no bundle declares one), and publication refuses a support provider as a candidate. Existing recursive integrity policy remains unchanged.

pinned_support.rule: Chip packages are not copied into Merlin. Each is pinned here by {target, repo, commit, tree} and fetched by commit (never by branch) with merlin-target-fetch <target> or its example's run.sh setup into out/build/generated/pinned/<target>@<sha12>/, verified against commit and tree. Every package layers on the ONE base pinned below: its provider.yaml extends.commit, and the gitlink of a base it carries as a submodule, must equal base.commit, or selection and fetch refuse it. Everything chip-specific lives in the chip repository's overlay (replace:/remove: included), never in a fork of the base. Editing a package: commit in <chip>-mlir, publish it, bump its one sha here (build_tools/scripts/vendor_support.py pin <target> <sha> also records the tree).
pinned_support.verification: merlin/tests/infra/test_support_pins.py: pins well formed, every package extends the base pin, the in-repo base copy records the base pin, fetch by commit, tree verification, and refusal of dirty, divergent and other-base checkouts, offline against local fixture repositories. core_references lists what each package's production code references in Merlin's core (build_tools/scripts/check_wiring.py counts it as a production caller); the test recomputes it from a fetched package.

vendoring.verification: merlin/tests/infra/test_example_support.py recomputes each vendored tree id from the tracked bytes, and the companion tree id with each normalized file's companion blob put back
vendoring.normalization: A vendored file may differ from its companion only where SOURCE.yaml lists it under normalized, with the companion blob id and the change. Absolute vendoring-host paths in provenance records are rewritten repo-relative there.
vendoring.scope: Targets whose support is still carried in-repo. The pinned_support packages are fetched, not vendored; the pinned base keeps its in-repo copy, whose SOURCE.yaml commit must equal base.commit.

Isolated explicit provider/oracle metadata imports, private support classification, synthetic runtime ABI/cache tests, and nine process-blocked codegen smoke cases. No native execution.
